newsitem.title: USA: Kmart to merge Canada functions; 150 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Kmart to merge Canada functions; 150 job cuts.

text.p: Kmart Corp. said Wednesday that it will merge many of its Kmart Canada business functions into its U.S. operations.
The move, which the giant retailer said was intended to maximize efficiencies, will result in 150 job cuts at the unit's head office in Brampton, Ontario by the end of the year.

Approximately 200 positions will remain in Canada and a number of new positions will be created in Troy, Mich., where Kmart is based, the company said. It was not specific about the number of new U.S. jobs.

"Following a thorough strategic review, Kmart determined that we can significantly strengthen the performance of Kmart Canada by streamlining its operations," said Thomas Watkins, chairman of the board of Kmart Canada.

"In recent months, Kmart Canada has significantly reduced inventory, improved merchandise assortments and instituted more effective advertising and marketing strategies," he said. "We intend to further capitalise on these improvements by making our Canadian stores more appealing to our customers."

Under the realignment, Kmart Canada's financial, systems, store operations and other administrative support functions will be merged into Kmart's headquarters in Troy, beginning in October. The merger will be completed in 1997.
Remaining functions in Kmart Canada's Brampton office will include executive management and merchandising functions, Kmart said.
Kmart's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $10.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
